maxillomandibular-advancement-mma.summary: Surgery that moves both jaws forward to project the lower face in profile and widen the airway, so you get a stronger profile and easier breathing together.

quick.overview:
MMA cuts the upper and lower jaws and moves them both forward. People want it for a stronger, more projected profile and, in the same operation, a wider airway behind the tongue and palate.

The forward movement pulls the attached soft tissue with it, which is what shows in profile and opens the airway. It began in orthognathic surgery and is now one of the most studied surgical treatments for obstructive sleep apnoea; a 2025 meta-analysis of 31 studies and 1,597 patients reported a mean fall of about 42 events per hour in the apnoea-hypopnoea index. Research on cosmetic outcomes is thinner than on sleep apnoea.
quick.how: People usually plan it with an orthodontist and a surgeon, often with 3D virtual planning, and it is typically considered after other sleep treatments such as CPAP have not worked. Forum users discuss it alongside midface expansion and rotation. Recovery is longer than for other sleep surgeries because the facial bones need time to heal, with the final shape settling over months.
quick.risks: A 2025 meta-analysis found early lower-facial numbness in about 83 percent of patients, lasting beyond a year in about a third, and hardware removal in about 22 percent. Other documented concerns are bleeding, airway swelling after surgery, relapse and jaw-joint problems. It is major surgery under general anaesthetic.

angle.text: MMA moves both jaws forward, so the profile projects further and the airway opens at the same time. Users see the change in profile once swelling settles. It is an established sleep-apnoea operation, and its cosmetic effects have been studied less.

jaw-surgery-orthognathic.summary: Corrective jaw surgery that repositions the upper jaw, lower jaw and chin to improve bite, breathing and facial balance, giving a stronger profile and straighter smile.

quick.overview:
Orthognathic surgery moves the upper jaw, lower jaw, chin or all three into a new position. People use it for a recessed jaw, an underbite or overbite, asymmetry and a better-balanced profile and smile.

Surgeons cut the jawbones from inside the mouth, move them to a planned position and fix them with titanium plates and screws, so bite, chin and midface realign together. Medical literature documents functional outcomes and technique well, and is more limited on purely cosmetic goals.
quick.how: It is coordinated with orthodontics, usually braces before and after, and planned with 3D imaging, custom splints and sometimes patient-specific plates. It is often combined with chin surgery or a nose operation. Recovery takes weeks to months, with swelling settling over that time.
quick.risks: Reviews describe bleeding, swelling, infection, nerve numbness, jaw-joint effects, relapse and hardware problems. A systematic review estimated that body dysmorphic disorder is more common among orthognathic patients than in the general community. It is major surgery performed by oral and maxillofacial surgeons.

angle.text: Orthognathic surgery repositions the jaws and chin, and forum users treat it as the major structural option for a recessed jaw, facial balance and a straighter bite and smile. The new jaw position is itself the visible result. Reports note that functional gains and cosmetic outcomes do not always match.

chin-implant-genioplasty.summary: Two ways to build out the chin, a placed implant or a cut-and-slid piece of jawbone, to balance your profile; bone sliding gives the larger change.

quick.overview:
Chin augmentation adds or repositions chin projection so the chin balances the nose and jaw in profile. The two main routes are an implant placed over the bone and a sliding genioplasty, where a section of the lower jawbone is cut and moved forward, back, up or down.

An implant adds volume at the front of the chin; a sliding genioplasty moves bone together with the tissue attached to it. Reviews describe a bone-based correction as usually giving a more dramatic result, while implants are the simpler operation. Published work covers techniques, materials and stability, with little head-to-head research on which looks best.
quick.how: Implants go in through an incision inside the lip or under the chin; genioplasty is done from inside the mouth with plates and screws. People often pair it with a nose operation or jaw surgery. Forum users debate how many millimetres of advancement to aim for. Swelling settles over weeks and the result is judged after healing.
quick.risks: Reported problems include swelling, hematoma, temporary lip or chin numbness, infection, implant displacement or bone changes under implants, nerve injury and asymmetry. Neither approach corrects the bite. Both are done by plastic, facial plastic or oral and maxillofacial surgeons as regulated surgery.

angle.text: Chin implants and sliding genioplasty add or reposition chin projection to balance the profile, and the change is visible after healing. Both are routine surgeries, and forums describe bone sliding as the larger change.

jaw-implants.summary: Implants placed along the angle and body of the lower jaw to widen and define it, giving a squarer, sharper jawline.

quick.overview:
Jaw implants, also called mandibular angle or gonial implants, are solid shapes of silicone, porous polyethylene or PEEK placed over the lower jawbone. People want them for a wider, more defined, squarer lower face.

The implant sits against the bone under the soft tissue, so the contour of the jaw looks wider at the angle and body. In published literature they appear mainly in facial gender-affirming surgery, where mandibular angle and body augmentation is described as a masculinising option, with one review reporting minimal complications and stating that more outcome research is needed.
quick.how: Placement is usually through an incision inside the mouth. Some designs are custom-made from CT scans. Forum users compare implants with bimax and genioplasty and talk about implant size, body fat and whether the underlying structure suits an implant. Swelling settles over weeks.
quick.risks: Reported concerns include a bloated or unnatural look when implants are too large or the structure is mismatched, soft-tissue sagging after removal, infection and displacement. Outcome data on cosmetic jaw implants are limited. They are placed by a surgeon under anaesthesia.

angle.text: Jaw implants add width and definition at the angle and body of the lower jaw, giving a squarer, sharper outline that shows once swelling settles. They are used in facial gender surgery and cosmetic work, and reviews note more outcome research is needed.

cheek-implants.summary: Solid silicone or polyethylene implants over the cheekbone that add projection for higher, more angular cheekbones; reviews report high satisfaction.

quick.overview:
Cheek implants are solid synthetic shapes placed on or under the cheekbone to make the midface more projected or fuller. People use them for flat cheekbones, asymmetry, ageing and facial feminisation, and looksmaxxers want higher, more angular cheekbones.

The implant sits over the malar bone, below it (submalar) or both, and fixed with sutures or screws, adding permanent volume unless removed. Reviews of the surgical literature report high patient satisfaction, with the evidence mostly retrospective series.
quick.how: Placement is through the mouth under anaesthesia. Users choose between malar and submalar shapes and between stock and custom implants. Swelling takes weeks to settle, and the shape is judged after healing. Some people also use fillers or fat as a softer alternative.
quick.risks: A 2025 meta-analysis of 3,701 patients found a 7.4 percent complication rate for malar implants (10.7 percent across facial implants), with high heterogeneity. Reported issues include infection, displacement, visible prominence and asymmetry. They are surgical devices placed by a surgeon.

angle.text: Cheek implants add projection over the cheekbone, giving higher, more angular cheekbones that are visible after healing. Reviews report high satisfaction, and the evidence is mostly case series rather than trials.

buccal-fat-removal.summary: Removal of the cheek's buccal fat pad through the mouth for a slimmer, more hollow-cheeked lower face; the change is permanent.

quick.overview:
Buccal fat removal takes out part of the deep fat pad in each cheek through a small cut inside the mouth. People want a slimmer lower face and a more visible cheekbone contour, especially if they stay round-faced even when lean.

Because the pad is not lost with general weight loss, proponents say removal changes contour where dieting does not. The pad does not regrow. Published evidence is mostly case series, a small single-arm trial and systematic reviews, and it became widely discussed on social media in the early 2020s.
quick.how: The pad is extracted by blunt dissection and suction through the intraoral incision, a short procedure. Swelling and stiffness go down over weeks and the final contour shows after that. Forum users compare it with facial slimming through leanness and discuss surgeon choice.
quick.risks: A 2025 meta-analysis of 308 patients reported a 25 percent prevalence of postoperative complications, mainly swelling, trismus, pain and asymmetry, with rare facial nerve paralysis, infection or hematoma. Parotid duct injury is reported. The effect is permanent and may look gaunt with ageing.

angle.text: Removing the buccal fat pad slims the lower cheeks for a leaner, more sculpted face, a permanent change that shows once swelling settles. A 2025 review reported a 25 percent pooled complication rate, and no randomised trials exist.

lateral-canthoplasty.summary: Surgery that tightens the outer eye corner, used medically for lid laxity and sought to lift the corner for a more upward canthal tilt.

quick.overview:
Lateral canthoplasty reshapes or tightens the outer corner of the eye by working on the lateral canthal tendon. Surgeons use it to support a loose lower eyelid, for ectropion and alongside lower blepharoplasty; looksmaxxers seek it for a more positive canthal tilt and a more almond eye shape.

The tendon is repositioned or tightened and anchored to the orbital rim, which lifts and supports the outer lid. The published literature covers lid support rather than cosmetic tilt, so changes in tilt for people with normal lid tone have not been studied.
quick.how: People discuss canthoplasty versus the gentler canthopexy, which supports the lid with sutures without detaching the tendon. It is often paired with lower blepharoplasty, and swelling settles over weeks before the shape is judged. Surgeons experienced in eyelid work do it under local or general anaesthesia.
quick.risks: Reviews note that small changes in this area can substantially alter lower eyelid shape, and that malposition, round-eye deformity and ectropion are risks. Self-performed versions discussed online have no published support.

angle.text: Lateral canthoplasty tightens and lifts the outer eye corner, which people seek for a more upward canthal tilt and an almond eye shape. It is an established lid-support operation, and no studies test it for that cosmetic goal.

hunter-eyes-surgery.summary: Community term for combined eye-corner surgery (canthopexy, fat grafts, blepharoplasty) aimed at a deep-set, positively tilted look.

quick.overview:
Hunter eyes is looksmaxxing shorthand for a deep-set eye with a positive canthal tilt and little lid show. The surgery people mean by it is usually canthopexy or canthoplasty, sometimes combined with fat grafting or blepharoplasty.

Canthal procedures reposition or suspend the outer lower lid; fat grafting adds volume under the eye or brow; blepharoplasty reshapes lid tissue. Together they aim to change tilt and lid exposure. The surgical literature studies these for lid support and rejuvenation, not for creating this look as a package.
quick.how: There is no single standard operation by that name, so people usually plan a combination with a facial or oculoplastic surgeon and bring reference photos. Swelling and bruising settle over weeks, and the final shape shows after months.
quick.risks: Reviews describe lid malposition, scleral show, ectropion and shape changes as risks, noting that small changes around the canthus can have large effects. Results as a combined cosmetic package are documented mostly in forum posts.

angle.text: Hunter eyes surgery combines procedures such as canthopexy, fat grafting and blepharoplasty to produce a deep-set, positively tilted eye look, visible after healing. The component surgeries are established, and no study tests the combined goal.

orbital-decompression.summary: Removal of orbital bone or fat so the eye sits further back for a deeper-set look; established for thyroid eye disease.

quick.overview:
Orbital decompression enlarges the eye socket by removing bone, fat or both, so the eye sits further back. Looksmaxxers discuss it as a way to get deeper-set eyes, with the eye position change visible after surgery.

Its established use is thyroid eye disease, where swollen muscle and fat push the eyes forward or threaten the optic nerve; surgeons remove parts of the orbital walls or fat so tissue has room to move backward. Trials and case series cover thyroid patients; none studies it for cosmetic deep-setting.
quick.how: Surgeons use endoscopic, conjunctival or other approaches, and decide between fat removal and bone work depending on the case. Forum users debate candidacy and technique. It is performed by orbital specialists under general anaesthesia, with weeks of recovery.
quick.risks: Reported complications in thyroid eye disease include optic neuropathy, corneal exposure, persistent double vision and raised eye pressure, and vision loss has been described in case reports. Forum posters call it among the riskiest hardmaxxing procedures.

angle.text: Orbital decompression lets the eye sit further back in the socket, which people want for a deeper-set look. It is an established thyroid-eye-disease operation, and cosmetic deep-setting has not been tested in trials.

blepharoplasty.summary: Eyelid surgery that removes or repositions excess skin and fat to reduce hooding and bags for fresher, more alert eyes.

quick.overview:
Blepharoplasty is the standard operation for droopy upper lids and lower-lid bags. It removes or repositions skin, muscle and fat so the eyes look more open, rested and alert, and it can also improve vision when lids obstruct sight.

Incisions in the lid crease (upper) or beneath the lashes or inside the lid (lower) allow removal, repositioning or preservation of tissue. Surgical literature supports it for dermatochalasis and bags, and a 2026 review described modern practice as shifting toward tissue preservation. East Asian double-eyelid surgery is one of the most common variants.
quick.how: People often combine it with fat grafts, brow work or canthal support, and looksmaxxers discuss it for eye shape and tiredness. Swelling and bruising last for weeks, and the final look settles over a few months.
quick.risks: Dry eye, lid malposition and asymmetry are reported complications, and surgeons often add canthal support to reduce malposition. Swelling and bruising are common for weeks. A 1987 infection cluster was traced to contaminated skin-marking solution.

angle.text: Blepharoplasty reduces upper-lid hooding and under-eye bags, giving fresher, more alert eyes once swelling settles. It is established for those concerns; looksmaxxing-specific eye-shape goals have not been tested in trials.

brow-lift-brow-bone-augmentation.summary: Surgical or injectable ways to raise the eyebrows or reshape the brow ridge for a more open, alert or masculine upper face.

quick.overview:
A brow lift raises a low or drooping eyebrow and can smooth forehead lines, opening up the eye area. Brow bone augmentation adds material over the ridge above the eyes for a stronger, more masculine brow, while reduction recontours a prominent one.

Surgical lifts release and reposition forehead and brow tissue, endoscopic versions use small scalp incisions, and botulinum toxin can raise the brow by weakening the muscles that pull it down. Bone augmentation uses implants, grafts or cement, and its published literature sits mostly in craniofacial and gender-affirming surgery.
quick.how: Options range from toxin and fillers to endoscopic, temporal and direct surgical lifts, and people often combine brow work with blepharoplasty, genioplasty or canthal surgery. Non-surgical options are temporary; surgical results settle over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Reviews describe scalp numbness, hair loss at incisions, hairline change, asymmetry, infection and bleeding, with technique-specific differences, and no technique is considered completely satisfactory in longevity. Forum participants discuss surgery abroad and the risk of poor results.

angle.text: Brow lifts raise a low or tired-looking brow, and brow bone augmentation builds a stronger, more masculine ridge; both changes are visible right after healing. Brow lifting is established for brow ptosis, while bone augmentation is documented mostly in reconstructive and gender-affirming work.

facial-masculinization-surgery.summary: Gender-affirming craniofacial surgery that builds up the forehead and brow and squares the jaw and chin, with techniques looksmaxxers borrow for a more masculine face.

quick.overview:
Facial masculinization surgery is a set of procedures that make the face read as more masculine: forehead and brow augmentation, jaw and chin augmentation, and Adam's apple enhancement. It is mainly performed as gender-affirming care for trans men and transmasculine people, and looksmaxxers borrow the toolkit for a squarer, more angular face.

Surgeons add or reshape skeletal and soft tissue with forehead implants, bone grafts, bone cement or fat; jaw angle and chin implants or osteotomies; and cartilage grafts. Planning often uses CT scans and virtual surgical planning with custom guides and implants. The literature is mostly reviews, case reports and book chapters.
quick.how: It is done as a planned set of operations with a craniofacial or facial plastic surgeon, sometimes in one session. Swelling settles over weeks and the skeletal change is visible once healed.
quick.risks: Complications depend on the procedure and include infection, implant movement or asymmetry, and nerve injury in jaw and chin work. The field has received less research attention than facial feminization.

angle.text: Facial masculinization techniques reshape the forehead, brow, jaw and chin for a squarer, more masculine face, visible once healed. The literature is mostly reviews and case reports from gender-affirming surgery rather than studies of appearance goals in cisgender men.

hair-transplant-fue-fut.summary: Surgical relocation of follicles from the back of the scalp to thinning or bald areas for a restored hairline and fuller hair; durable and well established.

quick.overview:
A hair transplant moves follicles from the back and sides of the scalp into thinning or bald areas, restoring a hairline and adding density. The two main harvesting methods are FUT, a strip of scalp dissected into grafts, and FUE, where individual units are taken with small punches.

Donor hair resists the hormone-driven miniaturisation of pattern baldness and tends to keep that behaviour after relocation, called donor dominance. A 2025 review called both FUE and strip excision state-of-the-art methods. Results depend on donor supply and surgeon skill.
quick.how: Grafts are placed in tiny recipient sites, shed over the first weeks and regrow over months, with the full result around a year. Many people combine surgery with medical therapy to protect native hair, and forums discuss timing relative to ongoing loss and clinic tourism to places like Turkey for lower prices.
quick.risks: Reported effects include swelling, itching, temporary numbness, donor-area scarring, temporary shedding of transplanted hair, folliculitis and infection. Native hair can continue to thin around transplanted areas. Quality varies widely between clinics.

angle.text: Hair transplants restore a hairline and add density where pattern hair loss has thinned the scalp, with grafted hair visible as it grows in. It is an established, durable procedure whose results depend on donor supply and surgeon skill, and forum posters often discuss timing relative to ongoing loss.

beard-transplant.summary: Follicular unit grafts moved to the jaw and cheeks to fill patchy or absent facial hair for a fuller beard.

quick.overview:
A beard transplant moves hair follicles, usually from the scalp, into areas of the face where beard growth is sparse or absent. Men use it to fill the jaw, cheeks and chin for a denser, more defined beard.

It uses the same graft-based techniques as scalp transplantation, with small recipient sites angled to match natural beard direction. A 2024 review by a surgeon with more than 700 primary beard transplants said restoring the beard has become an important part of hair restoration surgery because of its natural-looking results. The literature consists of surgeon series and expert reviews rather than controlled trials.
quick.how: Grafts of one or two hairs are harvested, trimmed and placed with the smallest possible blades, with angle and design chosen to look natural. Transplanted hair is expected to keep the traits of its donor area. Grafts shed and grow in over months.
quick.risks: General hair-transplant risks such as swelling, scarring and infection apply, and reviews discuss repair procedures for poor results. Choosing an experienced surgeon matters for natural angle and density.

angle.text: Men with patchy or absent facial hair use beard transplants to fill the jaw and cheeks for a fuller beard, which becomes visible as grafts grow in. Evidence consists of surgeon-reported series described in hair restoration reviews rather than controlled trials.

eyebrow-transplant.summary: Hair grafts placed in the brow to build denser or reshaped eyebrows; small surgeon series report high satisfaction.

quick.overview:
An eyebrow transplant moves individual hair follicles into the brow to thicken sparse brows, fill gaps or reshape them, giving the eyes a fuller, more defined frame. Surgeons describe the brow as small but demanding, because angle, direction, density and curl must match the natural pattern.

A 2021 case series of 36 patients using the long-hair follicular unit excision technique reported patient and surgeon scores of 4.7 and 4.3 out of five, and a 2024 study of 81 patients using hair from around the ear reported no significant complications over 15 months. No controlled trials exist.
quick.how: Follicular units are taken from the scalp or the area behind the ear and placed in small recipient sites angled to follow the brow. Long-hair extraction lets the surgeon see curl to match it. Grafts grow in over months.
quick.risks: Reported series describe few complications, but they are small and surgeon-authored. Mismatched curl, direction or density can look unnatural, and reviews describe corrective operations after unsatisfactory work.

angle.text: Eyebrow transplants thicken sparse brows or reshape them for a fuller, more defined eye frame, visible once grafts grow in. Small surgeon series report high satisfaction, and no controlled trials exist.

facial-fillers-jawline-chin-cheek.summary: Injectable hyaluronic acid or similar fillers that add projection to the jaw, chin and cheeks without surgery; temporary, adjustable and visible immediately.

quick.overview:
Facial fillers are injectable gels, most commonly hyaluronic acid (HA), placed under the skin to add volume or projection. People use them to sharpen the jaw angle, project the chin and lift the cheeks, sometimes called facial balancing, as a temporary and reversible alternative to implants.

The filler adds soft-tissue volume and, in firmer products placed deeper, structural projection. HA gives immediate correction and can be dissolved with an enzyme (hyaluronidase); other fillers include calcium hydroxylapatite and poly-L-lactic acid, which stimulates collagen over time. A 2023 Google Trends analysis found interest in jawline filler among men rose more than almost any other cosmetic procedure from 2004 to 2021.
quick.how: Clinicians inject it in a short appointment, and results show straight away, with swelling settling over days. It lasts months and is repeated to maintain. Forum members use it to test or approximate a stronger jaw before, or instead of, surgery.
quick.risks: Common effects include bruising, swelling, redness and lumps. Rare serious events include vascular occlusion with tissue necrosis and, in some regions, vision loss; reviews describe the jawline and several other areas as high-risk and high-reward. Fillers are regulated as medical devices and approvals vary by country.

angle.text: Fillers add volume at the jaw angle, chin and cheeks without surgery, so the contour sharpens and the face looks more defined and balanced straight after the injection. The change is temporary and adjustable, and fillers are well studied overall, though less so for young-adult contouring.

calcium-hydroxylapatite-filler-radiesse.summary: A dense, collagen-stimulating injectable filler used for firmer cheek, jaw and chin structure; studied mainly in ageing faces.

quick.overview:
Calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) filler, best known as Radiesse, is a gel containing tiny calcium-based microspheres. Clinicians inject it to add volume and structure to the cheeks, jawline and chin, and users like it for a firmer, more bone-like contour than softer fillers give.

The gel carrier gives immediate volume while the microspheres act as a scaffold, and reviews describe nearby cells producing collagen and elastin as the gel is gradually absorbed. A 2024 systematic review concluded CaHA may be considered a safe and effective option for the cheeks and jawline. Research mostly concerns older patients rather than young people seeking definition.
quick.how: Forum users discuss it as a 'high G prime' option for a defined jaw or chin without surgery. It is injected by a clinician in a short visit, with results visible straight away and refined over the following weeks as collagen builds. Many facial contouring uses are off-label.
quick.risks: A review of 21 studies covering 5,081 treatments reported adverse events in about 3 percent of treatments, almost all nodules. Fillers as a category carry a rare but serious risk of vascular occlusion, including blindness. In the US they are regulated as devices a provider must inject.

angle.text: Radiesse is a dense filler that gives firmer jaw, chin and cheek structure straight away, and is reported to stimulate collagen over time. Trials have mostly involved ageing faces rather than young-adult contouring.

black-market-diy-fillers.summary: Filler bought outside regulated channels and used without a clinician to add jaw, chin or lip structure cheaply; carries the filler risks with no safeguards.

quick.overview:
Black-market or DIY filler means dermal filler products people obtain outside licensed medical channels and use on their own faces. On looksmaxxing forums it is presented as a low-cost way to add structure to the jaw, chin or lips without visiting a clinic.

Fillers in general work by adding volume at the injection site, and hyaluronic acid gels of different firmness are used for structure or to soften transitions. The forum material consists of user guides and personal plans, not research. Published sources describe fillers given by trained providers, and no studies of self-injection were identified.
quick.how: Users describe sourcing products online and planning their own routines, mostly with hyaluronic acid-type gels. Details are left out here; people who want filler results can get the same product class through a licensed provider, who can also dissolve hyaluronic acid filler if needed.
quick.risks: Reference sources describe bruising, redness and pain as common, and rare but serious complications including blindness when material reaches the eye's arteries, usually permanent when it occurs. In the US, fillers are devices that a provider must inject. Forum posters themselves discuss vascular occlusion and nerve injury, and unregulated products have no quality checks.

angle.text: People buy filler outside clinics and self-inject to add jaw, chin, cheek or lip structure cheaply, with the contour change visible straight away. Filler is well studied when clinicians give it; the self-injection practice rests on forum accounts.

masseter-botox.summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the jaw muscle to shrink it over months for a slimmer, softer lower face; temporary and repeated.

quick.overview:
Masseter Botox is botulinum toxin type A injected into the masseter, the main chewing muscle at the angle of the jaw. The goal is to weaken it so it shrinks, slimming a wide or boxy lower face. It is also used for teeth grinding and jaw pain.

The toxin blocks the nerve signal to the muscle, and with less use the masseter loses bulk over weeks. Reviews report reduced muscle bulk and reshaped lower face with minimal, short-lasting adverse effects, and several company-sponsored randomised trials for masseter prominence have been run. Use for appearance has been off-label.
quick.how: A clinician injects it in a short visit with little downtime. Results build over weeks and wear off after months, so people repeat it to maintain. Forum users say it suits some face shapes better than others.
quick.risks: Injecting the masseter can reduce chewing ability, and toxin spread can weaken unintended muscles; asymmetry has been reported. Researchers have examined whether reduced chewing load changes jawbone density; one placebo-controlled trial found no clinically significant change, while a smaller radiograph study in bruxism patients found region-specific reductions in a bone texture measure.

angle.text: Masseter Botox relaxes the jaw muscle so it shrinks over weeks, slimming a wide or boxy lower face. It is reasonably studied for muscle prominence, results are temporary, and a 2025 trial is the main data on effects on the bone.

lip-filler.summary: Injected gel that adds lip volume and definition straight away; well documented in trials and temporary.

quick.overview:
Lip filler is the injection of a gel, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), to add lip volume, define the border or balance the upper and lower lip. It is one of the most widely performed non-surgical cosmetic treatments, and randomised multicentre trials have compared HA lip products head to head.

HA gels bind water and add volume where injected, and reviews call HA the gold standard lip filler because it is biocompatible and reversible. Fat transfer, collagen and permanent fillers are other methods with different durations. Some forum posters argue that mouth width matters more than fullness and that filler cannot widen the mouth.
quick.how: A clinician injects it in a short visit with results visible straight away, and swelling settles over days. It lasts months and people repeat it to maintain, often starting with a small amount and adding over time.
quick.risks: Swelling and bruising commonly last up to a week. Reviewers of lip safety describe complications that can be severe, note they are underreported, and say prospective randomised safety trials are lacking. Overfilling can look unnatural, and HA filler can be dissolved if needed.

angle.text: Lip filler adds volume, defines the lip border and balances upper and lower lip, with the change visible straight away. It is temporary and well documented in trials; some forum rating systems weigh mouth width more heavily than lip fullness.
